clue.text: Resurrected revolutionary costume in navy

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right over, so the word for costume is read backwards

parts.note: a robe is a costume or garment

explanation.surface: A revolutionary uniform brought back to life inside the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' signals the garment word is reversed; 'in' places that inside the navy abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resurrected has been brought back to life, i.e. given a second birth.

clue.text: Rose maybe better initially turning to right

indicators.note: the first letter of the word changes into the letter that follows

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: A rose that improves at first before veering right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'improved' but means one who bets, GAMBLER; 'initially turning to' swaps its G for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a climbing variety of rose, so it is an example of one, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Fight apparently no longer postponed having shown ability to draw an audience

definitions.text: having shown ability to draw an audience

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists
something postponed is 'on ice', so jokingly no longer postponed is 'off ice'

explanation.surface: A boxing match that was delayed finally goes ahead and proves a crowd-puller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' flags the playful reading: the opposite of 'on ice' (postponed) is OFF ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A box-office show or star has proved commercially popular, selling plenty of tickets.

clue.text: Far-off meteor exploded

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so the letters of meteor are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A distant meteor has blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' rearranges METEOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote is a synonym for distant, a long way away.

clue.text: After Church two of Henry's wives take in Latin passages

indicators.note: the wives come after the church abbreviation, so it leads the answer
the two wives take in, i.e. hold, the Latin letter inside them

parts.note: Henry VIII married two Annes, Boleyn and of Cleves

explanation.surface: After church, two of Henry VIII's wives absorb some Latin texts.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII had two wives called Anne (Boleyn and of Cleves), hence ANNES; 'take in' puts L inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Channels are narrow waterways or ducts, i.e. routes through which something passes.

clue.text: Assist some simple-hearted characters ascending

indicators.note: in a down clue ascending means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
some of the characters says only a run of letters inside the clue words is wanted

explanation.surface: Aiding a few naive people as they rise in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks PLEH out of simPLE-Hearted; 'ascending' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to aid them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Negative about America including Indian region in restricted zone

indicators.note: the outer pieces include, i.e. enclose, the region placed in them

parts.note: no is a negative reply
re means about or concerning
Goa is a state on India's west coast

explanation.surface: A refusal regarding America containing an Indian state inside a closed area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' marks the containment; the Indian state slips in straight after the negative.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a place where entry is forbidden or unsafe, a restricted area.

clue.text: Echo expression of disapproval king gives publication

parts.note: E is Echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
boo is a jeer of disapproval
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king gives a book that gets an echoing boo.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-book is a digital edition of a book, so a published work.

clue.text: Slippery fish returning quietly with queen is secret agent

indicators.note: returning means the word for the fish is read back the other way

parts.note: eels are notoriously slippery fish
p (piano) means quietly in music
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Slippery fish come back quietly with royalty, which is how a spy operates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns EELS into SLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a spy planted long in advance and kept inactive until needed.

clue.text: Wounds covering cross gnomes

indicators.note: the outer word covers, i.e. encloses, the cross mark

parts.note: maims means wounds or injures
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: Wounded garden gnomes covered by an angry cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnomes' looks like garden figures, but it is the plural of gnome, a pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in this sense is a short aphorism, so gnomes are sayings or proverbs.

clue.text: Advertise GAP outlet

parts.note: to plug a product is to advertise it
a hole is a gap

explanation.surface: An instruction to promote a branch of the clothing chain Gap.
explanation.walkthrough: GAP in capitals poses as the retailer; it simply means a hole, and 'outlet' is a drain, not a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A plughole is the drain opening of a basin or bath through which water flows away.

clue.text: Mischievous child learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: A naughty child is learning how to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead or entreat earnestly.

clue.text: The seven ages of man in two sentences

definitions.text: The seven ages of man in two sentences

parts.words: The seven ages of man in two sentences
parts.note: the whole span of existence, expressed as two prison terms joined: getting life and doing time

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's seven ages of man summed up in a couple of sentences.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'sentences' as prison terms: a life sentence and doing time, put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaques' seven ages of man speech traces the whole span of a human existence.

clue.text: Rugby player happy to provide support

parts.note: a back is a rugby player behind the forwards
up means happy or cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: A cheerful rugby player gives his teammates support.
explanation.definitionFit: Backup means support or reinforcement held in reserve.

clue.text: Dog or horse or something moved by mouse

definitions.meaning: a breed of gun dog that stands still aiming its nose at game
a point-to-..., a horse ridden in point-to-point races, is shortened this way
the arrow on a computer screen that the mouse moves around

explanation.surface: Listing creatures a mouse might push about, the joke being a computer mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouse' suggests an animal beside the dog and horse, but it is the computer device.
explanation.definitionFit: On screen the cursor arrow is called this; the dog breed points at game birds.

clue.text: Storyteller returning to complain bitterly

indicators.note: returning means the word for the fibber is read backwards

parts.note: a storyteller in the sense of a fibber, a liar

explanation.surface: A storyteller coming back to grumble bitterly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' suggests a narrator, but here it means someone who tells lies.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily or rant against something.

clue.text: Great hotel rebuilt entirely

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of the two words are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A great hotel has been completely reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges GREATHOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is a synonym for completely or wholly.

clue.text: I eat meat prepared with bit of horseradish as source of iron

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just its opening letter
food that is prepared is made up, so these letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Eating meat with horseradish as a dietary source of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives the H of horseradish; 'prepared' rearranges IEATMEAT plus H.
explanation.definitionFit: Haematite is the chief ore from which iron is extracted.

clue.text: Informed about hot husband regularly at it somewhere in China

indicators.note: the informer's word goes about, i.e. around, the letter for hot

parts.note: sang is slang for informed on someone to the police
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Telling tales about a hot-tempered husband who's regularly at it in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H inside SANG; 'regularly' picks A and I from 'at it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is a major city in China, so it is one place there.

clue.text: Going on about French and English articles held by force

indicators.note: the articles are held inside the word for force

parts.note: to bring someone to do something is to force them
le is the French definite article
the is the English definite article

explanation.surface: Rambling about French and English grammar being held by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' marks the containment; to bring someone to do something is to force them.
explanation.definitionFit: Blethering is talking at length about nothing much, chattering on.

clue.text: Fastens bottom on top of seat

parts.note: butt is informal for bottom

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone does up their trousers by putting their bottom on a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' takes the S of seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To button something is to fasten it, so this is the verb form for securing clothing.

clue.text: Some most extraordinary words

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark about some quite remarkable words.
explanation.definitionFit: A text is a body of written words, so it stands for the words themselves.

clue.text: Cause great pain to people in unlawful act

indicators.note: in tells us the people go inside the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men stands for people in general

explanation.surface: Hurting people through a criminal act.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to inflict severe suffering on them.

clue.text: Book size

definitions.meaning: a single bound tome in a series
the amount of space something occupies, its capacity

explanation.surface: A bookseller's terse note on a book's dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: one book of a set, and a measure of three-dimensional space.

clue.text: Empty theatre and church having no musical style

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Deserted theatres and churches with no music played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves TE from theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a form of electronic dance music with a fast repetitive beat.

clue.text: Disengaged and cold Shakespearean king

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's chilly old king, cut off from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disengaged' means free or unhindered here, as in clear of obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear can mean free of entanglement, as when a gear is disengaged or someone steers clear.

clue.text: Elegant posh girl broadcasting live

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, an upper-class young woman
on air describes a programme being broadcast as it happens

explanation.surface: A stylish upper-class girl is being broadcast live.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave, stylish and charming, much like smart or polished.

clue.text: Silent Greek character outside of Thule

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A quiet Greek figure beyond the far northern land of Thule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' gives TE from Thule.
explanation.definitionFit: Mute means making no sound, unable or unwilling to speak.

clue.text: Recondition surplus loot

parts.note: over means left over, in surplus
a haul is a thief's loot

explanation.surface: Restoring something with surplus stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to strip it down and repair it thoroughly.

clue.text: Pointless fellow with posh hat

parts.note: U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A fellow sporting a fancy hat to no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class usage; tile is dated slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile means ineffective or useless, achieving nothing.

clue.text: Maintains Army and Navy

definitions.meaning: keeps a car or machine in working order

explanation.surface: Something keeps the armed forces going.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for routine upkeep and for the armed forces collectively.

clue.text: Exclusive group includes heads of Labour Education Committee

indicators.note: the group includes, i.e. holds inside it, the initial letters

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: heads of means the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: An elite group includes the leaders of a Labour education committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Select means choice and exclusive, open only to a chosen few.
